samples: This module reads a JSON configuration file from a given path and checks that it fits the expected shape: a valid port (1 to 65535), 1 to 64 workers, and a log level of quiet, normal or verbose. If the file can't be read or doesn't match, loading fails with an error saying which problem occurred. It also provides a built-in default (port 8080, 4 workers, normal logging) and a function that falls back to a configuration you supply when loading fails, while an older fallback function is deprecated in favor of that one.

This module reads a JSON configuration file for a service and checks it against a fixed shape: a port from 1 to 65535, a worker count from 1 to 64, and a log level of quiet, normal, or verbose. If the file can't be read or doesn't match, loading fails with an error that says which problem occurred. It also provides built-in defaults (port 8080, 4 workers, normal logging) and a fallback-loading function that uses either your own configuration or the defaults when loading fails. The older default-fallback function is deprecated in favor of the one that takes your own fallback configuration. The only permission it needs is read access to the filesystem.

This module reads a service's JSON configuration file and checks that it has a valid port (1–65535), a worker count (1–64), and a log level of quiet, normal or verbose. If the file can't be read or doesn't match that shape, it fails with an error saying which problem occurred, and it only needs read access to the filesystem. It also supplies a default configuration (port 8080, 4 workers, normal logging) and a function that falls back to a configuration you choose when loading fails. An older fallback-to-defaults function is deprecated, so you should use the newer one.

This module reads a JSON configuration file for a service and checks it against a fixed shape: a port between 1 and 65535, 1 to 64 workers, and a log level of quiet, normal or verbose. If the file can't be read or doesn't match, loading fails with an error that says which problem occurred. It also provides built-in defaults (port 8080, 4 workers, normal logging) and a loader that falls back to a configuration you supply, while an older default-based loader is deprecated in favor of that one. It only needs permission to read files.

This module reads a JSON configuration file for a service and checks it against a fixed shape: a port from 1 to 65535, a worker count from 1 to 64, and a log level of quiet, normal or verbose. If the file can't be read or doesn't match, loading fails with an error that distinguishes the two cases. It also offers a built-in default setup (port 8080, 4 workers, normal logging) and a loader that falls back to a configuration you supply, while an older fallback-to-default loader is deprecated in favor of that one. The only permission it needs is read access to the filesystem.
